text:
Ajay: running a nvprof/nvvp capture inside the inference container to investigate a perf regression in kernel selection. getting permission errors when nvprof tries to write /tmp/nvprof*.

Ajay: container is k8s pod with nvidia-container-toolkit, runtimes configured. we mount /tmp and host /dev/nvidia* devices via the daemonset.

Maria: error text?

Ajay: `nvprof: can't create file '/tmp/nvprof-12345.nvprof': Permission denied`

Kevin: is the process running as non-root in the container? most nvprof/Nsight tools write to /tmp and need the user to have write perms or for /tmp to be rw inside the container.

Ajay: yes, we run as appuser (uid 1001). /tmp is root:root 1777 inside the image, but when mounted from host it's root:root 755 (weird) — probably host-mount masking the sticky bit.

SRE-Jordan: when k8s mounts a hostPath without specifying fsGroup, permissions show as on host. If /tmp was created on the node with 0755 it loses the sticky bit. Quick workaround: `securityContext: { runAsUser: 0 }` or `initContainer` to `chmod 1777 /tmp`.

Ajay: can we avoid running as root? prefer not. any nvidia-container-toolkit-specific constraints?

Maria: nvprof/Nsys open output files with default umask and expect world-writable tmp. Alternatively use `--output-file` and point to a known writable dir in the container filesystem (non-hostPath) or write to stdout and capture.

Kevin: also be careful about container seccomp and capabilities. Tools that attach to GPU or host tracing may require CAP_SYS_PTRACE or access to /proc/sys/kernel/yama ptrace_scope=1. For nsys attach mode you might need elevated privileges or run as root inside the container.

Ajay: tried `--output-file /app/tmp/trace.nvvp` -> fails, app dir is read-only. mounting an emptyDir at /var/tmp and giving appuser ownership is probably the right path.

trace-bot: Uploaded trace to https://internal-artifacts/trace/1787554321/nvprof-raw. nsys timeline indicates a spike in cuBLAS kernel selection fallback around t=23s (lots of small GEMM dispatches).

Maria: that matches batch profile changes — batching heuristics started producing many shorter sequences after the recent scheduler tweak. short sequences trigger a different kernel path (small GEMM) that falls back to a slower kernel on current driver.

Kevin: suggestion: rerun with synthetic workload to reproduce: run inference with controlled batch sizes 1,2,4,8 and capture nsys with `nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx -o out` or nvprof with `--profile-child-processes --output-file`. capture kernel timelines: `nsys stats out.qdrep --report=gpu-kernels`

Ajay: tried that. nsys shows that for batch=1 we hit cuBLAS kernel id 0xabc slower by ~3x vs batch=8 which uses a tuned GEMM. nvprof output: `cuBlasGemmEx` calls but different algorithm picks.

SRE-Jordan: driver/toolkit versions matter. There are known heuristics in cuBLAS/cuBLASLt that pick fallback kernels depending on shapes and alignment; newer drivers change selection. Make sure container's cuda/driver/kernel modules match node host driver. mismatch can cause perf cliffs.

Ajay: nodes run driver 525.x, container runtime has CUDA 11.8 libs baked in. confirm host-driver compatibility?

Maria: check `nvidia-smi` inside the pod and on the node; also `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version`. If libs in container are older/newer than host driver, cuBLAS may still function but algorithm selection can differ.

Kevin: also look at alignment/padding of tensors. KV cache layout changes recently: we switched to column-major KV buffer to reduce copies, but that can change leading dim and trigger non-optimal GEMM algos.

Ajay: good call — KV cache change was rolled out last week. Rolling back locally to previous layout removes the regression in our synthetic runs.

Maria: for long-term fix: either teach batching heuristics to produce shapes that favor the faster kernel or add a kernel-selection shim that forces cuBLAS algorithm via `cublasSetMathMode`/`cublasLt` heuristics, OR ship a small alignment pad so leading dims are favorable.

SRE-Jordan: operationally: update k8s pod spec to use an initContainer to `chown` the emptyDir to appuser, keep non-root runtime, and add a job to collect traces nightly with proper permissions (init sets 1777 on host-mounted tmp if needed).

Ajay: will try initContainer + synthetic profiling across batch sizes and send results. thanks for the pointers. :thumbsup:

trace-bot: New trace uploaded: https://internal-artifacts/trace/1787554321/nsys-batch-sweep.qdrep

Kevin: once you have the nsys qdrep, run `nsys export --format sqlite out.qdrep` and inspect `gpu_kernel` table to compare durations and algorithm ids. I can write a small script to diff kernel selections across traces.

Ajay: dropping results here when done. planning to open a short PR to revert KV layout until we have tuned kernel selection.

Maria: please also add a regression test: small-batch perf should not drop >20% on the most common sequence lengths. we can automate nightly profiling and alert on regressions.

Ajay: will add test and follow up with results.

Kevin: if you need help with the chown initContainer or the nsys -> sqlite pipeline ping me.

Ajay: thanks everyone.
